How it works

Five years shape the next one

Every annual naming group copies names from the preceding five years or invents a dataset-shaped name. Invention stays anchored to observed names while recent inventions contribute to later forms.

Where numbers come from

NYC dog licensing data

Records are aggregated into approximate annual naming groups for each NYC area and mapped using official ZCTA boundaries.

In each simulated year, names are either copied from the previous five years—locally or citywide—or invented by a character-based Markov model that learns letter patterns from observed and recent simulated names. Invented names are filtered for readable length, pronounceability, repetition, and a maximum of four syllables.

What it cannot see

A cultural sketch, not a forecast

  • Owner intention, language, ethnicity, income, or social networks
  • Unlicensed dogs, renaming, adoption, or movement
  • Actual pronunciation, meaning, harm, or cultural appropriateness
  • Future population, licensing, geography, or media changes
One stochastic run is one possible future, not a prediction. All data, geometry, styles, scripts, and the OFL-licensed Modak display typeface are embedded in this file.
